title: FormData API concept and file upload boundaries
learningObjectives: Explain formdata api concept and file upload boundaries and create accessible, secure form behaviour.

understand.concept: The FormData interface represents form fields as name/value entries and can be built from a form or populated in JavaScript. File inputs can contribute File objects. Sending files requires server-side size, type, content, and authorization checks.
understand.whyItMatters: Client-side file metadata and accept hints can be manipulated. Upload endpoints must enforce limits, inspect actual content, and store files safely. Do not expose private storage paths or trust filenames.
understand.analogy: FormData is a package of labelled values; a selected file is an object in that package, not proof that the file is safe.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual validation, submission, and assistive technology behaviour follow browser and platform rules.

explain.narrative: The script lists form entries and shows the selected file name for learning only. A real upload needs a trusted server endpoint and validation.

examples.explanation: The script lists form entries and shows the selected file name for learning only. A real upload needs a trusted server endpoint and validation.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered form example demonstrating the HTML behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Extend the example to show file name and size, then document the server-side checks required before storage.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible form with labels, constraints, clear errors, and a documented server-side validation plan. Test keyboard use and invalid values.
hints: Do not rely on colour or placeholder alone.
Client-side checks do not provide authorization or security.
Keep errors associated with their fields and easy to locate.

questions.prompt: Does a client-side accept attribute prove that a file is safe?
questions.explanation: The server must validate the actual uploaded content and enforce limits.

questions.prompt: Which form approach is most reliable?
options: Accessible client feedback plus authoritative server validation
questions.answer: Accessible client feedback plus authoritative server validation
questions.explanation: Good forms combine user-friendly browser feedback with trusted server-side enforcement.
